neighboring_unit_entries.title: Complex path deformation localizes the moderate spectral range
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: For moderate real spectral parameters, deforms the hypergeometric integral onto a short segment plus a tilted ray, obtains exponential damping on both pieces, and combines this with the large-parameter estimate to restrict the spectral analysis to a finite T-dependent window.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Uniform saddle extraction for the negative Maass range
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Locates the saddle, deforms the inner contour into negligible tails plus a steepest-descent segment, proves uniform truncation and Taylor control including the Gaussian weight, evaluates the resulting Gaussian, and applies a second saddle computation to the outer integral to obtain the oscillatory kernel with explicit damping.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The asymptotic proof first removes holomorphic, large, small, and positive spectral ranges by uniform contour estimates, leaving a negative Maass window in which a two-stage saddle calculation yields the oscillatory main contribution; a spectral mean-value estimate then controls aggregation error.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The localized ranges depend on sufficient smoothing hypotheses chosen partly for simplicity and are not claimed optimal.
